title: Acute Otitis Media
text: Subject: Acute Otitis Media. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Patient complains of severe right ear pain, fever, and mild hearing loss. Otoscopic exam shows bulging, erythematous tympanic membrane with loss of landmarks. Diagnosed with acute otitis media. Prescription: Amoxicillin 875mg twice daily.

title: Streptococcal Pharyngitis
text: Subject: Streptococcal Pharyngitis. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: A 14-year-old presenting with acute onset of sore throat, fever of 102F, and painful swallowing. Exam reveals tonsillar hypertrophy with exudates and anterior cervical lymphadenopathy. Rapid strep test positive. Prescription: Penicillin V.

title: Chronic Sinusitis
text: Subject: Chronic Sinusitis. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Adult male with a 3-month history of facial pressure, nasal congestion, and purulent postnasal drip. CT scan shows mucosal thickening of maxillary and ethmoid sinuses. Recommended saline rinses and fluticasone nasal spray.

title: Acute Tonsillitis
text: Subject: Acute Tonsillitis. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Patient presents with high fever, sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and muffled voice. Examination shows enlarged erythematous tonsils with bilateral exudates. Throat culture obtained. Advised rest, hydration, and acetaminophen.

title: Cerumen Impaction
text: Subject: Cerumen Impaction. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Elderly patient presenting with progressive bilateral hearing loss and sensation of ear fullness. Otoscopy reveals complete occlusion of both external auditory canals with dark, hard cerumen. Successfully cleared with irrigation.

title: Allergic Fungal Sinusitis
text: Subject: Allergic Fungal Sinusitis. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Patient with chronic sinus congestion, anosmia, and nasal polyposis. Allergic mucin containing eosinophils and fungal hyphae retrieved during sinus debridement. Treatment: surgical ventilation and oral steroids.

title: Vocal Cord Nodule
text: Subject: Vocal Cord Nodule. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Professional singer presenting with persistent hoarseness and vocal fatigue for 6 months. Laryngoscopy reveals bilateral symmetric vocal cord nodules at the junction of anterior and middle thirds. Referred for speech therapy.

title: Vestibular Neuritis
text: Subject: Vestibular Neuritis. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Sudden onset of severe vertigo, nausea, vomiting, and gait instability. Horizontal-torsional nystagmus beats towards the unaffected ear. Negative head-impulse test. Treated with methylprednisolone taper and meclizine.

title: Laryngopharyngeal Reflux
text: Subject: Laryngopharyngeal Reflux. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Patient reports chronic throat clearing, persistent dry cough, globus sensation, and hoarseness. Laryngoscopy shows interarytenoid erythema and vocal fold edema. Initiated Omeprazole 20mg twice daily.

title: Acute Epiglottitis
text: Subject: Acute Epiglottitis. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Pediatric patient presenting with sudden high fever, sore throat, drooling, and stridor. Sitting in tripod position. Muffled voice. Immediate airway management initiated. IV Ceftriaxone and dexamethasone administered.

title: Peritonsillar Abscess
text: Subject: Peritonsillar Abscess. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Severe unilateral sore throat, fever, trismus, and deviation of the uvula to the opposite side. Fluctuant swelling of the soft palate. Needle aspiration performed, yielding 4cc of purulent fluid. Treated with IV antibiotics.

title: Nasal Septal Deviation
text: Subject: Nasal Septal Deviation. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Patient complains of chronic unilateral nasal obstruction and recurrent epistaxis. Examination reveals severe cartilaginous deviation to the left, occluding 80% of the airway. Scheduled for septoplasty.

title: Conductive Hearing Loss
text: Subject: Conductive Hearing Loss. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Young adult with progressive hearing loss in left ear. Weber lateralizes to left, Rinne negative on left. Consistent with otosclerosis. Discussed stapedectomy vs. hearing aid.

title: Temporomandibular Joint Disorder
text: Subject: Temporomandibular Joint Disorder. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Patient complains of jaw pain, clicking sounds, and headache, particularly in the mornings. Tender masseter muscles. Managed with night guard, NSAIDs, and soft food diet.

title: Salivary Gland Sialolithiasis
text: Subject: Salivary Gland Sialolithiasis. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Swelling and severe pain in the submandibular region, worsening during meals. Palpable stone in Wharton's duct. Stone massaged out of duct orifice. Advised hydration and sialogogues.

title: Acute Laryngitis
text: Subject: Acute Laryngitis. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Loss of voice and tickling throat sensation following a viral upper respiratory infection. Vocal cords erythematous and edematous. Recommended voice rest, hydration, and humidification.

title: Nasal Polyps
text: Subject: Nasal Polyps. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Bilateral nasal congestion, hyposmia, and mouth breathing. Examination reveals pale, translucent masses in nasal cavities. Managed with fluticasone spray and oral prednisone taper.

title: Eustachian Tube Dysfunction
text: Subject: Eustachian Tube Dysfunction. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Patient reports popping/clicking sounds in ears, pressure changes, and autophony after air travel. Retracted tympanic membrane. Managed with decongestants and Valsalva maneuver.

title: Labyrinthitis
text: Subject: Labyrinthitis. Clinical Presentation and Assessment: Patient presents with acute onset of vertigo, tinnitus, and sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear following a viral illness. Treated with prednisone, valacyclovir, and vestibular rehabilitation.

title: Angina Pectoris Case Study 1
text: Patient is a 45-year-old male presenting with Chest pressure radiating to left arm, precipitated by exertion and relieved by rest or nitroglycerin. ECG shows transient ST depressions.. Blood pressure: 120/80 mmHg. Heart rate: 70 bpm. Diagnostic Workup confirms Angina Pectoris.

title: Myocardial Infarction Case Study 2
text: Patient is a 48-year-old female presenting with Crushing substernal chest pain radiating to neck and jaw, accompanied by diaphoresis and dyspnea. Troponin levels elevated. ST elevation on ECG.. Blood pressure: 127/84 mmHg. Heart rate: 75 bpm. Diagnostic Workup confirms Myocardial Infarction.

title: Atrial Fibrillation Case Study 3
text: Patient is a 51-year-old male presenting with Palpitations, lightheadedness, and irregular pulse. ECG confirms irregularly irregular rhythm without P waves. Anticoagulation started.. Blood pressure: 134/88 mmHg. Heart rate: 80 bpm. Diagnostic Workup confirms Atrial Fibrillation.

title: Congestive Heart Failure Case Study 4
text: Patient is a 54-year-old female presenting with Bilateral pitting pedal edema, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and jugular venous distention. Echocardiogram shows EF of 35%.. Blood pressure: 141/92 mmHg. Heart rate: 85 bpm. Diagnostic Workup confirms Congestive Heart Failure.

title: Essential Hypertension Case Study 5
text: Patient is a 57-year-old male presenting with Asymptomatic elevation of blood pressure measured at 165/95 mmHg on three separate occasions. Advised lifestyle modifications and Lisinopril.. Blood pressure: 148/96 mmHg. Heart rate: 90 bpm. Diagnostic Workup confirms Essential Hypertension.

title: Aortic Stenosis Case Study 6

title: Mitral Valve Prolapse Case Study 7

title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
text: Subject: Vertigo. Description: BPPV presents with brief episodes of vertigo (spinning sensation) associated with changes in head position. Diagnostic test: Dix-Hallpike maneuver eliciting geotropic nystagmus. Precaution profile: Avoid sudden head movements, sleep with head elevated on two pillows, avoid bending down to pick up items, and perform Epley maneuver under guidance.

title: Foreign Body in Upper Aerodigestive Tract
text: Subject: Foreign Body. Clinical scenario: Patient (often pediatric) presents with sudden onset of choking, dysphagia, or stridor. In ENT contexts, a foreign body (e.g., small toy, coin, or fishbone) may be lodged in the auditory canal, nasal cavity, or pharynx. Immediate examination and extraction using forceps or laryngoscopy is required. Complications include airway obstruction or perforation.

title: Pediatric Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)
text: Subject: Croup. Clinical scenario: A child aged 6 months to 3 years presents with a characteristic barking cough, inspiratory stridor, and hoarseness, typically preceded by coryza. Etiology: Parainfluenza virus. Severe cases show intercostal retractions. Treatment: Single dose of oral Dexamethasone, nebulized epinephrine for stridor at rest, and cool mist therapy.

title: Allergic Rhinitis
text: Subject: Allergic Rhinitis. Clinical scenario: Patient complains of seasonal or perennial sneezing, rhinorrhea, nasal congestion, and itchy, watery eyes. Pale, boggy turbinates. Driven by IgE-mediated response to allergens. Treatment includes second-generation oral antihistamines (e.g., Cetirizine), intranasal corticosteroids, and allergen avoidance.
